Blessing Bearer

Passives
[Passive - Toggle] Thought Acceleration —
Increases movement, attack and chanting speed. Mastering Blessing Bearer improves movement/attack bonuses and adds dodge invulnerability, following native Thought Acceleration configuration.

[Passive - Toggle] Self Regeneration —
Heals each second while injured. Mastery improves healing and also restores spiritual health. Uses the native Self Regeneration magicule cost with its own regeneration cycle. Pauses when energy is insufficient or healing is blocked.

Both passives use Blessing Bearer's toggle, without needing an active slot. They are calculated independently and do not grant extra skill entries or change existing standalone skills, their toggles, mastery or effects.

Active Modes
[Active - Press] World Blessing —
Spend 30 experience levels to draw an unowned blessing from the 15-entry pool. Associated resistances reach 100% mastery. Chat announces the blessing and native skill acquisition messages.

[Active - Press] World Response —
Switch Blessing Bearer's mode to list collected blessings in chat. Cooldown: 3 minutes. No experience cost.

[Active] Blessing of Martial Arts
Each successful draw costs 6 Magic Ore Shards and 60 XP levels. 35 equally likely, non-repeating blessings; no cost on completion or failure. Native skills gain full mastery. World Response lists both collections. Custom passives follow the Bearer toggle; native rewards retain their own toggles.

Sword Saint - Reinhard

Embedded Thought Acceleration bonuses are doubled. Self Regeneration is replaced with embedded Ultraspeed Regeneration: every half second, restore missing physical health using the native magicule cost and mastery discount. Insufficient magicules restore only the affordable portion. It creates no standalone skill or shared effect and does not restore spiritual health. Blessing potion levels are doubled (Strength V to X, Speed II to IV, Luck V to X, Haste II to IV), including cooking, water breathing and phoenix effects. Durations, cooldowns, costs, native standalone skills, enchantments and other blessing bonuses are unchanged.

While toggled on, grants immunity to native Anti-Skill and clears existing Anti-Skill. Other status/area rules are preserved. The hidden sword passive is inherited without granting another sword. World Response retains its 3-minute cooldown.

With Sword Saint, Dragon Sword removes 0.5 maximum health per point of actual health damage from non-player enemies, until death (minimum maximum health: 1). After defeating a recognized enemy or leaving its 16-block detection radius, returns to the matching sheath after 10 seconds without a recognized enemy nearby. Reentry cancels the countdown; leaving again starts a new 10-second countdown.
Phoenix prevents one death per 10 minutes, including /kill and direct physical/spiritual death. It restores full magicules without a totem overlay. A death sequence within one server tick consumes one charge. Dragon Sword also recognizes non-player mobs with learned Unique/Ultimate skills or over 2000 maximum HP within 16 blocks, regardless of their toggle.
While enabled, also blocks and removes Silence, Anti-Magic and Magic Interference. Recovers 300,000 magicules per second, capped at maximum, with no additional doubling. This recovery is exclusive to the ultimate skill.

Reincarnation lock

The ten essences recorded by older versions count toward thirty; unrecorded consumption cannot be reconstructed. Retain this skill, blessing collection, their learned native rewards, mastery and cooldowns through reincarnation while locked. Manually unlocking disables retention; the bonus slot is awarded only once.

Dragon Essence loot
Melee kills with your own drawn Dragon Sword add three essences for Ice and Fire cave dragons. Other non-player creatures have a 10% base chance to drop 1-3 essences, plus two percentage points per Looting level, capped at 100%. Fortune blessing supplies Looting V; take the higher level instead of adding levels. Cave dragons do not receive the random reward as well.

Accessories are items that can be combined with equipments to grant unique properties. Each accessory can only be combined with a specific type of equipment.
The number of accessories an equipment can hold depends on the number of accessory slots it possesses. You can combine or separate accessories from equipment just as you would place or remove items from a bundle. Additionally, combining can be done directly through crafting. Accessories may be obtained from mobs or chests. Additionally, some accessories have unique acquisition methods.

The Accumulator is a redstone device that can receive redstone signal from one direction and output it in all other directions.
Among its six faces, the one marked with a red dot is the input face, while all other faces are output faces. As the input signal strengthens, the color of the Accumulator gradually shifts from gray to blue.

A machine that uses the teeth of Thirst Walkers as its core material, inheriting the Thirst Walker's greed.
Upon receiving a redstone signal, it can use the crystals in it to infest nearby environments and collect the resources contained therein.

A weapon crafted using the teeth of Thirst Walkers, the materials used to make it allow it to absorb nutrients to increase its sharpness.
It seems to retain activity and a primal need for food, so much so that he may act out and betray its master in cases of extreme hunger.

Stranghouls use it to dry rotten flesh into leather for their armor.
It can be placed over a campfire, at which point the rotten flesh can be placed to obtain Rotten Flesh Jerky, which is tastier but harder to chew than rotten flesh.

The Energy Transmitter is a redstone device capable of transmitting redstone signal over long distances.
To use it, first interact with the emitter end, then with the receiver end to establish a connection between the two. Once linked, the Energy Transmitter will emit a beam of light between the emitter and receiver while active.
The emitter collects redstone signal from the block it is attached to and transmits them wirelessly, while the receiver passes the received signal to the block it is attached to.

In ancient times, they had been the embodiment of the frozen magic of this dimension. The discovery of the Freeze provided a major opportunity for the ancient Starlighters when they were building that mechanical giant and realized that the exothermic heat of the machine was too intense but could not be solved due to technical problems.
The Freeze were modified and eventually used successfully for cooling and defense against intruding enemies, and the magical ice ball they once shot were compressed and sealed in tubes.
You can defend yourself against their intensive attacks using cold-proof armor.
A plant infused with the power of the moon's radiance by an ancient civilization, used to devour the souls of prisoners held in the labyrinth.

Normally, its resilient epidermis significantly reduces all incoming damage.
However, when ignited or stunned, it loses this damage reduction ability.
As a plant, it remains immobile most of the time, but will occasionally burrow underground to pursue its prey.

Meteor showers sometimes occur here. During the meteor shower, countless meteors streak across the night sky, creating a beautiful sight. But there is also danger in the beauty, be careful not to get hit by the large meteorites. After dodging them, you can find some ores at the landing spot. Creteors may spawn after the large meteorites land, you can kill them to get their hide. You can also build an Aethersent Golem to prevent meteors from destroying your home, or use Aetherstrike Rockets to cause meteor showers manually.

Nocturnal Millet is a crop native to the Starlight Dimension, whose seeds are hidden within Thioquartz at the banks of the Ether River.
Nocturnal Millet seeds can be sown on dirt, farmland, or Dusted Gravel. Once the stalks have grown, the tops will naturally produce panicles.
When the panicles are plump and ripe, interacting with them will grant Nocturnal Millet. The stalks will remain after harvesting, but there is also a small probability that they will wither. Withered Nocturnal Millet will continuously destroy other types of crops nearby. If a stalk loses its vitality, applying bone meal can revive it.
If Nocturnal Millet is planted on Dusted Gravel and bone meal is applied to the stalk, the entire plant will enter a state of forgotten. Panicles in this state no longer produce ordinary Nocturnal Millet, but instead condense into Forgotten Nocturnal Millet. Plants in the forgotten state will seize the life force of other types of crops nearby to accelerate their own maturation. These types of panicles are exceptionally tough and can only be obtained by interacting with them. Destroying them with brute force will yield nothing.

A mysterious orb that knows all.
It can be used on the portal frame to open the portal.
Beside from this, you can access all of your crests and cast spells with them.
To cast a spell, first check the requirements of the spell you want to cast and make sure you have one of the mana crystals that can be accepted.
Then, hold the orb and switch to that spell you want to cast.
Lastly, you're ready to use the orb to cast the spell.

Following the Starlighters' successful conversion of Freezes into cooling units, they soon realized the latent magical energy within these constructs far exceeded their initial projections. By fusing and augmenting multiple Freezes, they forged the ultimate thermal regulator: the Permafrost.
If the Freeze is a mere network of cooling vents, then the Permafrost is a surging pump of liquid nitrogen. As the definitive evolution of its predecessor, it retains the primal instincts of the Freeze while wielding absolute dominion over frost.
Long after the civilization crumbled into dust, this machine remains among the ruins, mechanically executing its final directive: to bring the world to absolute zero.

A fruit found everywhere in the Dark Swamp that tastes somewhat like garlic, it gives off an odor that makes people weep, which allows it to be made into a weapon as well.
A stew made of it and rotten flesh can rid you of hunger effect, but such food doesn't seem to be very tasty.

This unique weapon can shoot seeds of any type at high speed, it is made primarily from Pungency Fruits, but the exact method of production is unknown, so the only way to obtain it is to barter with their makers.
The weapon can be enchanted, and when enchanted it can shoot seeds with unique properties.
A magical eye that can be used to locate the ruins where the powerful creatures live. You need to hold a locator item too if you wish to find a specific structure.

An insect that flits around shimmer river and dark swamp with four pairs of glowing blue or purple wings. Their presence is neither threatening nor useful to other creatures. When the Starlight civilization still existed, this was a small creature loved by children.

A precious food made from Pungency Fruit and Deepsilver Ingots that still retains the flavor of Pungency Fruits. It paralyzes your nerves, causing your body to temporarily ignore most damage, but all damage is still returned after a period of time.

Mechanical creations built by the ancient Starlighters to do the bidding of the mechanical giants used to defend against the doom, once possessing heavy armor and unparalleled strength.
To this day, no intact golems exist.

Under normal circumstances, its armor is difficult to penetrate.
However, when it stops attacking and begins to absorb energy, its weakness becomes apparent.

§8[[An explorer's notebook that seems to have survived an explosion]]§0

This tower clearly has mechanisms that are not responding to me. Their magic almost yearns to acknowledge my touch, but it cannot. It is if the devices of the tower are being

suppressed by a powerful group of beings nearby.

§8[[Next entry]]§0

The magic seems to emanate from deep within the strongholds nearby. It can't come from the goblins, as their magic is charming, but unfocused. There

must still be some force still active in the strongholds.

§8[[Next entry]]§0

My analysis indicates that it comes from several sources, operating as a group. I will head back to the stronghold after I resupply...

§8[[An explorer's notebook, written on fireproof paper]]§0

Fire is a trivial obstacle for a master explorer such as myself. I have traversed seas of fire, and swam through oceans of lava. The burning air here is an interesting variation, but

ultimately no hindrance.

What does stop me though is that I have encountered another protection spell, this time surrounding a mighty creature that must be king of this fire swamp. This is not the first protection spell I have encountered, and I am

beginning to unravel the mysteries of how they work.

If this spell is like the others, it will be sustained by a powerful creature nearby. Surrounding the fire swamp are several wet swamps, and under those swamps are labyrinths full of minotaurs.
The logical choice to bind such a spell to would be some sort of powerful minotaur, different in some way from the others that surround it...

§8[[An explorer's notebook, caked in ice]]§0

I overcame one blizzard, only to run into this terrible ice storm atop the glacier. My explorations have shown me the splendor of an ice palace, shining with the colors of the

polar aurora. It all seems protected by some sort of curse.

§8[[Next entry]]§0

I am no novice. This curse is fed by the power of a creature nearby. The cause of the curse surrounding the fire swamp was built off the power of the

leader of the minotaurs nearby.

Surrounding this glacier, there are masses of yetis. Perhaps the yetis have some sort of leader...

§8[[An explorer's notebook, written on waterproof paper]]§0

The mosquitoes in this swamp are vexing, but strange. The vast majority of them seem to have no natural source, nor do they seem to have a role in the local ecology. I have begun to suspect that they are

some kind of magical curse.

§8[[Next entry]]§0

Now that I have encountered a protection spell on the ruined labyrinth here, I consider my suspicions confirmed. Both the protection spell and the mosquitoes are a

curse. This curse seems to have a different source from the others I have encountered. I will have to research further...

§8[[Next entry]]§0

The curse seems to be of a type too powerful for one being alone to

produce. Several wizards working in combination would be necessary.

If one of the wizards stopped contributing, the whole of the curse over the entire swamp would fall. Strangely, my divinations do not show signs of any nearby living wizards.
I did see something interesting in one of the nearby pointy-roofed towers though...

§8[An explorer's notebook, gnawed on by monsters]§0

I have begun examining the strange aura surrounding this tower. The bricks of the tower are protected by a curse, stronger than any I've seen before. The magic from the curse is boiling off into the

surrounding area.

In my homeland I would have many options for dealing with this magic, but here my supplies are limited. I shall have to research...

§8[[Many entries later]]§0

A breakthrough! In my journeys I sighted a huge snake-like monster in a decorated courtyard. Nearby, I picked up a worn down, discarded green scale.

The magic in the scale seems to have the curse-breaking
properties I need, but the magic is too dim. I may need to acquire a fresher specimen, directly from the creature.

§8[[An explorer's notebook, written on faintly glowing paper]]§0

The tendrils of darkness surrounding this area are just a manifestation of a protective spell over the entire dark forest. The spell causes blindness, which is quite vexing. I have seen several

interesting things in the area and would like to keep exploring.

§8[[Next entry]]§0

I have found ruins in the dark forest. They belong to a stronghold, of a type usually inhabited by knights. Rather than knights though, this stronghold is full of

goblins. They wear knightly armor, but their behavior is most un-knightly.

§8[[Next entry]]§0

Deep in the ruins, I have found a pedestal. The pedestal seems to be of a type that knights would place trophies on to prove their strength.

Obtaining a powerful scepter would seem to weaken the curse on the dark forest, and placing a trophy associated with a powerful creature on the pedestal would likely grant access into the main part of the stronghold.

§8[[An explorer's notebook, damaged by acid]]§0

There seems to be no way to protect myself from the toxic rainstorm surrounding this area. In my brief excursions, I have also encountered another protection spell, similar to the others I have

witnessed. The spell must be connected to the toxic storm in some way. Further research to follow...

§8[[Next entry]]§0

Such supreme weather magic must be the result of multiple undefeated great evils in this world. My studies contain
several clues pointing at a searing swamp, a forest coated in deep darkness, and a realm coated in snow.

§8[[This book shows signs of having been copied many times]]§0

I cannot explain the field surrounding this structure, but the magic is powerful. If this curse is like the others, then the answer to unlocking it lies elsewhere. Perhaps there is something I have left
undone, or some monster I have yet to defeat. I will have to turn back. I will return to this place later, to see if anything has changed.

§8[[An explorer's notebook, covered in frost]]§0

The blizzard surrounding these snowy lands is unceasing. This is no ordinary snowfall--this is a magical phenomenon. I will have to conduct experiments to find what is capable of

causing such an effect.
